title: SPAD Flash LiDAR with Chopped Analog Counter for 76m Range and 120klx Background Light
problem: Flash LiDAR using single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) must simultaneously achieve long range (76m), high depth resolution, and high frame rates under strong background light (120klx) without performance degradation.
motivation: Automotive, space, and robotic applications require robust 3D sensing that tolerates bright sunlight and complex backgrounds while maintaining depth accuracy at extended range.
method: The sensor shoots light pulses and measures how long they take to bounce back to calculate distance (direct time-of-flight). It uses ultra-sensitive light detectors called single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) that can count individual photons. The sensor uses a 'chopped analog counter'—a circuit that suppresses background-light interference by rapidly toggling the measurement on and off—to work in extremely bright conditions (120,000 lux). It builds a histogram of photon arrival times to create a depth map at 76 meters' range at high frame rates.
key_novelty: The chopped analog counter design—which suppresses background-light interference by alternating measurements on and off—enables robust depth sensing at 76-meter range under extreme brightness (120,000 lux).
contributions: 76m range capability with high depth resolution under 120klx background light
Chopped analog counter suppressing background-light-induced noise
Compact pixel pitch with improved fill-factor compared to prior dToF designs
limitations: Pixel-level performance metrics not specified in abstract.
